correctness.rationale: A cyclic word corresponds exactly to an Euler tour of ordered distinct pairs linked by ordered distinct triples. The unique 012 window removes position rotations without modding out alphabet labels. To verify exhaustion independently, assign at each of the twelve overlap vertices a bijection between its two incoming and two outgoing arcs. The resulting permutation of 24 arcs is a valid Euler tour iff it has one orbit. Conversely each valid cycle gives one such assignment. Among all 4096 assignments this gives 384 words. Independent normalization by lexicographically least cyclic rotation and exhaustive tests of all 24 relabelings with and without reversal reproduced each per-permutation fixed count, the 20 and 11 quotients, the joint orbit sizes, and all 20 rows of classes.tsv, including self-mirrors 6 and 10. Burnside gives (384+96)/24=20 and (384+96+48)/48=11. No stabilizer can contain two alphabet transpositions since their product is another excluded type. The 96 cycles with a relabeling stabilizer therefore give eight orbits of size 12; the other twelve have size 24.
residual_risks: Exhaustive only for these four symbols and the injective length-three factor condition. The count 11 uses the joint action, not reversal alone.

value.rationale: Changing the letter names or orientation does not change the underlying construction, so their quotients are motivated directly by the cycle definition. This determines exactly which minimal nontrivial cases are essentially different, including nontrivial stabilizers and the two self-mirror classes. It supplies canonical test objects for permutation universal cycles and their Gray-code versions, data that cannot be reconstructed by dividing the established labeled total by group order.
residual_risks: Finite classification at one natural alphabet size; no larger-order orbit formula or downstream theorem is implied.
